i0: The verb must **agree** with its subject: a **singular** subject takes a **singular** verb (*She **works***), and a **plural** subject takes a **plural** verb (*They **work***).
i1: This is easy with short subjects, but harder with words like *everyone, each* and *one of*, and with long subjects. For group nouns like *team* and *family*, see [Plural Nouns](/blog/grammar/plural-nouns/#pn-group-nouns).
sva-basic.t: He works, they work; there is, there are
sva-basic.s: In the present, use **-s** with *he, she, it* and singular nouns (*My brother works*). With *I, you, we, they* and plural nouns, there's no *-s* (*My brothers work*). Use **there is** + singular and **there are** + plural.
sva-basic.b1: ***There is*** + singular or uncountable noun: *There **is** a bank. There **is** some milk.* ***There are*** + plural: *There **are** two banks.*
sva-basic.b2: The past of *be* also changes: *I / he / she / it **was***; *you / we / they **were***. And ***has*** with *he, she, it*: *She **has** a car.*
sva-everyone-each.t: Everyone is, each student has, one of my friends is
sva-everyone-each.s: ***Everyone, everybody, someone, nobody, everything*** take a **singular** verb (*Everyone is here*). So do ***each*** and ***every*** + noun. ***One of*** + plural noun also takes a **singular** verb (*One of my friends lives in Paris*).
sva-everyone-each.b1: The verb agrees with ***one***, not with the plural noun after *of*: ***One** of the students **is** late.*
sva-everyone-each.b2: After *everyone / someone*, we often use *they / their* to refer back: *Everyone **has** **their** own room.*
x.sva-everyone-each-b04: *One of the* + plural noun + singular verb.
